experiments.lesson: Design flaw: a 0.5 probability threshold with a 38.8% positive base rate selected almost nothing (3 validation, 4 holdout trades). Selection must be rank-based or calibrated to the base rate.

experiments.evidence: scripts/research-ml-external.js (pre-registered 869a9bb9e); daily manifest dd81586b...; external.json sha256 9f49c83a9d366acf8be5d41cdca543b8a7c6fe6cfdbb604faa5830ed74a50f26
experiments.lesson: No skill: adding the BTC Korea premium and global BTC momentum left the model unchanged in effect (holdout -0.771% per trade vs universe -0.467%, 1,755 trades). Linear daily cross-sectional ranking of KRW markets consistently picks losers (likely high-volatility names).

No skill: 355 holdout trades, -0.404% per trade vs universe +0.271% (win 42.5%). Four ML models in a row picked markets that did worse than the market average on unseen data; the inverse is NOT a valid conclusion because it was seen on the holdout (it may only be tested on forward data).

experiments.evidence: scripts/research-ml-trades-flow.js (pre-registered 026562ac4; fetch-only fix 8958a6f8a); 7 days of public Upbit trade ticks 2026-10-06..12, 30 markets; manifest files sha256 3a51fc0205b0da5ffbe38fa23ac75c9b95f91c9b2fa45a0243611b01a359ddb6
experiments.lesson: Order flow did not transfer: validation (1 day) +0.026% per trade vs universe -0.082%, but holdout (2 days, 144 trades) -0.532% vs universe -0.279%, win 33.3%, p 0.998. Fifth ML model in a row to pick worse-than-average markets on unseen data. Only 7 days of ticks exist publicly, so splits are tiny; the universe was re-selected after a transient HTTP 503 during the first fetch (same rule, fetch-time ticker).
